To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
eggs of different species of ratites differ in terms of their physical parameters, VM, and the composition of its proteins.

the ostrich egg is characterized by the highest yolk content (yolk weight and yolk ratio) and the lowest yolk pH and water activity, the emu egg has the highest yolk water activity, whereas greater rhea eggs have the highest yolk pH and the lowest consistency index.

ostrich eggs are the heaviest, emu eggs have the highest yolk index, ostrich and emus yolks have the highest consistency index and the lowest flow behavior index, and greater rhee yolks have the strongest VM.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a comparative analysis of morphological traits and selected physicochemical properties of eggs of ostrich, Emu, and greater Rhea.
the morphological, structural, and physical properties of ostrich, greater rhea, and emu egg yolks and the structure of their VM.

the first comprehensive comparative analysis of selected morphological traits and the physical and mechanical properties of eggs and yolks, as well as the structure and composition of VM, of ostrich, greater rhea, and emu.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ostrich and emus are more similar than ostrich and greater rheas.
the VM of greater rhea egg yolk was the most resistant, and the VM of emus was the most elastic.
the structure of the eggshell and yolk of the ostrich, emus, and greater rheas are different.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the VM of ostrichi eggs had the highest resistance to breaking and the lowest water activity, whereas the VMs of emu and great rhea eggs were the most resistant to breaking and had the highest water activity, respectively, and the yolks of ostrichi eggs and the VM of greater rhea yolks were characterized by the lowest and highest breaking force, respectively.
the VM of greater rhea yolks was characterized by the most diverse structure, the highest breaking force, and the highest number of protein bands.
the ostrich and emus have the highest egg and egg yolk weight compared to the greater rhea.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the VM of ostritch eggs was the most elastic, that of greater rhee eggs the most resistant and that of emu eggs the most diverse in terms of structure.
the structure and strength of the VM, as well as the physical parameters of yolks, differ significantly between species.
the structure and strength of the VM and the composition of proteins of the VM of the ratites are species‐dependent.
